title: Becky Hammon on Jalen Brunson’s Knicks’ title run: ‘He’s an outlier’
content:
LAS VEGAS — Becky Hammon isn’t apologizing.

Nearly three years ago, she said on ESPN that New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson was “too small” to be the first option on a championship team. After he proved otherwise, leading New York to its first NBA title in 53 years, Hammon didn’t move off from the evaluation she made at the time.

“All he did was prove history wrong,” Hammon said. “He proves he’s an outlier, so you can put his name next to Steph Curry and Isiah Thomas.”

In 2023, Hammon was asked on “NBA Today” about the Knicks’ championship potential. She emphasized the team’s lack of star power, saying the best teams in the league have a “1A dude” and that the Knicks lacked a player of that caliber.

The three-time WNBA championship-winning coach acknowledged Tuesday that Brunson played “brilliantly” during the 2026 postseason and did call him a “1A dude.” But she’s not saying sorry.

“Apologize?” Hammon said. “I’m never going to apologize for having an opinion. That’s what ESPN pays me for.”

In Hammon’s view, the Nova Knicks were a team of destiny. She commended their performance in the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs and even drew parallels between herself and Brunson.

Hammon went undrafted in the 1999 WNBA Draft before signing with the New York Liberty as a free agent. She went on to have a 16-year playing career, becoming a six-time All-Star and the league’s 2007 assist champion, but she never won a championship as a player. The closest Hammon came was with the Liberty when they lost in the WNBA Finals to the Houston Comets in 1999 and 2000 and the Los Angeles Sparks in 2002. She advanced to the finals with the San Antonio Silver Stars, now the Las Vegas Aces, in 2008, but they lost to the Detroit Shock in a three-game sweep.

The Dallas Mavericks selected Brunson with the 33rd pick in the second round of the 2018 NBA Draft.

“When you talk about comps, who’s comparable to him?” Hammon asked. “Who does he play like? Never seen anybody like him. The guy is 6-1 and bullies a 6-7 league on average. And he bullies people on offense.”

Hammon said she has always been a Brunson fan, going back to his days at Villanova, where he won two NCAA championships. Three years after her initial remarks, she is still confused about how her take went so far “off the rails.”

But she still had one more button to push with Knicks fans.

“Let me just piss Knicks fans off again and say I think he’s the greatest Knick ever,” Hammon said. “Give them something else to talk about.”
